newsitem.title: UK: Intimate photos show Diana romance for real.
newsitem.headline: Intimate photos show Diana romance for real.

text.p: British newspapers pronounced on Sunday that Princess Diana had finally found love with hazy photographs showing her locked in a passionate embrace and talk of a winter wedding.

The man captured kissing and hugging Diana is Dodi Fayed, 41-year-old son of Harrods department store boss Mohammed Al-Fayed, during a "secret" cruise in the Mediterranean the couple enjoyed this month aboard his Egyptian father's luxury yacht.

"Locked in her lover's arms, the princess finds happiness at last," the Sunday Mirror newspaper said in eight pages devoted to the new saga in Britain's royal soap opera. "Now Dodi flies off to buy an engagement ring for Diana."
Speculation about Diana's love life soared last week amid talk of a bidding war for "intimate" shots of the 36-year-old princess, one year after her divorce from Prince Charles, 48.
While fuzzy, the pictures clearly show a couple in swimsuits caressing, hugging, kissing and lounging on deck, apparently oblivious to any onlooker.

"See how she gives herself up to her new lover. How she nestles her head trustingly against his muscular chest," said the Mirror. "Our world exclusive photos show that, after years of inner turmoil and tears, Princess Diana has finally found a man who makes her feel like a real woman."
Although the Mirror won the photo bidding wars, its rivals too proclaimed a new turn in Diana's turbulent life and said the affair, this time, was for real.
"Diana and I are having a romance. A true romance," the News of the World quoted Dodi as telling his ex-wife.
"It's not a fling, I promise. It's serious," he reportedly told Suzanne, a 33-year-old American model to whom he was briefly wed in 1986.
A Di and Dodi marriage, should it ever come, would be quite a coup for his father, who has often clashed with the British establishment.
The princess, in Bosnia this weekend to help promote an international campaign against landmines, has maintained a public silence about jet-setting Dodi but friends said she was ready for marriage.
"The next time I see him I am expecting an engagement ring," the Mirror quoted the "besotted" princess as telling friends.

It said an engagement announcement could come as early as next month, followed by a lavish party and, perhaps, a winter wedding for the fun-loving woman whose "fairytale" union with the austere House of Windsor turned exceedingly sour.
The princess has kept her diary free from November "suggesting Diana and Dodi could be man and wife in the New Year," said the Mirror.
Her friends were quoted as saying Diana would quit buttoned-up Britain for a new life in the easy-going United States, where Dodi works as a film producer.
In many ways, it is a perfect match.

Dodi -- who owns homes around the world and has dated stars from Brooke Shields to Britt Ekland -- enjoys the high life that Diana craved during her dour marriage and friends say she is finally having fun. As for him, there is the obvious attraction of dating one of the world's most watched, and watchable, women.
Her former in-laws are reportedly happy for Diana to start a new life, even though his friends say it would take quite a woman to make Dodi settle down.
Diana's sons too, in line to the throne after Charles, have apparently given their blessing but would have to remain in Britain as key members of the royal circle, the papers said.
